subject.title: Feature Request: Abstract file scanning pipeline as Memory Plugin API

question: What public memory-ingestion SDK contract should OpenClaw support for third-party memory plugins that need file indexing from MEMORY.md, memory/, and extraPaths?
rationale: The requested behavior adds public plugin API surface and changes the local-file trust boundary, so implementation should follow maintainer-approved semantics rather than the issue's callback sketch by default.

options.title: Design a Narrow SDK Seam
options.body: Add a reviewed memory-ingestion contract with explicit file scope, event batching, delete semantics, chunking ownership, and compatibility tests before external plugins consume it.

options.title: Expose Helpers Only
options.body: Keep list/read helpers as the supported surface and let memory plugins own their own watchers and stale cleanup, accepting backend-specific drift.

options.title: Defer File Indexing for External Memory
options.body: Leave external memory plugins conversation-only until memory plugin architecture converges on a recommended backend path.

recommendation.title: Design a Narrow SDK Seam
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed memory-ingestion contract with explicit file scope, event batching, delete semantics, chunking ownership, and compatibility tests before external plugins consume it.

likelyOwner.reason: The memory slot, memory-core extraction, and memory host SDK extraction history make Peter Steinberger the best available owner for the API direction call.
